case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread discusses how to correctly qualify products using Nordic nRF52 series SoCs and third-party modules such as BM832 under Bluetooth SIG QPRD v3 rules. The main focus is whether products built with nRF Connect SDK 2.8.0 can reuse existing Nordic qualification assets and avoid additional qualification fees. The discussion also evaluates whether BM832 must continue referencing its original SoftDevice-based QDID 97989 or can instead use newer nRF Connect SDK BLE 5.3 and Mesh qualification references. The final outcome clarifies that qualification eligibility depends on the implemented firmware stack and referenced QDIDs rather than the physical module alone.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread explains that BM832 itself does not own an independent QDID and instead references Nordic End Product QDID 97989 built from older SoftDevice SDK 5.0.0 component declarations. The discussion compares qualification reuse for products built with nRF Connect SDK 2.8.0 versus products built with older SoftDevice SDK object code. It also clarifies that products using qualified nRF Connect SDK 2.8.0 object code on nRF52 series SoCs can be added as derivative products without additional qualification fees, including some third-party module implementations. Bluetooth Mesh support under the newer SDK qualification scope is also discussed. The exchange distinguishes between hardware reuse and Bluetooth stack qualification reuse.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The core qualification decision is driven by the implemented Bluetooth stack and object code rather than the module hardware itself. A product may reuse newer Nordic qualification references if the actual implemented firmware matches the qualified nRF Connect SDK 2.8.0 scope and corresponding QDIDs. Older SoftDevice-based declarations cannot automatically cover products running different SDK implementations. Derivative product reuse is valid only when the Bluetooth implementation remains within the same qualified SDK and declaration scope.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: If a product ships with firmware built from a different SDK than the referenced QDID or declaration, the Bluetooth qualification may become invalid. Incorrectly assuming that a module hardware QDID automatically covers all future firmware implementations could lead to declaration errors, compliance exposure, or requalification work. Misunderstanding derivative product eligibility could also cause unnecessary qualification fees, duplicate submissions, or incorrect Product List registrations.
case_analysis.consulting_mistake: An early interpretation suggested that BM832 qualification reuse was restricted because the module referenced QDID 97989 tied to the older SoftDevice SDK. Later clarification from the module supplier confirmed that BM832 hardware could instead be qualified using the newer nRF Connect SDK 2.8.0 qualification references when the implemented firmware matched that SDK scope. The correction highlights the importance of separating hardware identity from firmware qualification scope.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When evaluating Bluetooth qualification reuse, always verify which Bluetooth stack, SDK version, and object code are actually implemented in the product. Module hardware alone does not determine qualification eligibility; the declaration must match the implemented qualified software stack and referenced QDIDs.
